description: PBR textures for the Tbilisi residential-complex zombie shooter. Each set is assets/textures/<set>/{color,normal,roughness,ao}.jpg. All maps tile seamlessly; normal maps are OpenGL (+Y), which three.js expects.
threejs_usage: Set colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace on color maps only; the other maps are linear. Use wrapS = wrapT = THREE.RepeatWrapping and set repeat from tile_size_m (world metres per texture repeat). Since r151 aoMap uses the primary UVs.

asphalt.description: Worn, fine-grained grey road asphalt with faint hairline cracks (city road).
asphalt.author: ambientCG (Lennart Demes)
asphalt.normal_convention: OpenGL (+Y up, green = up), the three.js default
asphalt.normal_convention_verified: G channel correlates 0.938 with the source height-map gradient (positive = OpenGL)
asphalt.notes: ambientCG gives no physical size; judging by the aggregate grain, about 2.5 m per repeat looks right.

concrete.description: Smooth light-grey concrete for sidewalks, curbs and plinths.
concrete.author: ambientCG (Lennart Demes)
concrete.normal_convention: OpenGL (+Y up, green = up), the three.js default
concrete.normal_convention_verified: G channel correlates 0.927 with the source height-map gradient (positive = OpenGL)
concrete.notes: Non-square 1024x512 texture covering 1.10 m x 0.55 m; repeat about 0.91 x 1.82 times per metre.

pavers.description: Grey interlocking concrete pavers (zig-zag or "dogbone" uni-stones), typical of modern Tbilisi courtyards.
pavers.author: ambientCG (Lennart Demes)
pavers.normal_convention: OpenGL (+Y up, green = up), the three.js default
pavers.normal_convention_verified: G channel correlates 0.789 with the source height-map gradient (positive = OpenGL)
pavers.notes: The source has no AO map (ambientCG PavingStones099 ships color, normal, roughness and displacement only).

pavers_alt.description: Warm red or salmon interlocking concrete pavers of the same dogbone family as "pavers", with some moss in the joints. Use for paths, borders or accents.
pavers_alt.author: ambientCG (Lennart Demes)
pavers_alt.normal_convention: OpenGL (+Y up, green = up), the three.js default
pavers_alt.normal_convention_verified: G channel correlates 0.751 with the source height-map gradient (positive = OpenGL)

grass.description: Short, dense lawn grass with natural colour variation.
grass.author: ambientCG (Lennart Demes)
grass.normal_convention: OpenGL (+Y up, green = up), the three.js default
grass.normal_convention_verified: G channel correlates 0.556 with the source height-map gradient (positive = OpenGL)

soil.description: Dry brown dirt with clods and small stones, for tree pits and the wasteland edge.
soil.author: Rob Tuytel
soil.normal_convention: OpenGL (+Y up, green = up), the three.js default
soil.normal_convention_verified: G channel correlates 0.749 with the source height-map gradient (positive = OpenGL)
soil.notes: The 1.3 m source tile is small, so scale it up (for example 2.5 m) or break up repetition on large areas.

gravel.author: ambientCG (Lennart Demes)
gravel.normal_convention: OpenGL (+Y up, green = up), the three.js default
gravel.normal_convention_verified: G channel correlates 0.807 with the source height-map gradient (positive = OpenGL)

plaster.description: Clean, matte, smooth light facade plaster or stucco with subtle trowel mottling.
plaster.author: ambientCG (Lennart Demes)
plaster.normal_convention: OpenGL (+Y up, green = up), the three.js default
plaster.normal_convention_verified: G channel correlates 0.791 with the source height-map gradient (positive = OpenGL)
plaster.notes: ambientCG gives no physical size; about 2–3 m per repeat is suggested. The source has no AO.

stone_cladding.description: Beige travertine square stone tiles or panels, usable as light stone facade cladding.
stone_cladding.author: ambientCG (Lennart Demes)
stone_cladding.normal_convention: OpenGL (+Y up, green = up), the three.js default
stone_cladding.normal_convention_verified: G channel correlates 0.792 with the source height-map gradient (positive = OpenGL)
stone_cladding.notes: About 6x6 squares per tile (about 33 cm each at the source scale). Scale by 2 for 60–70 cm facade panels. The source has no AO.

pool_tiles.description: Small bright-blue pool tiles with grey grout.
pool_tiles.author: ambientCG (Lennart Demes)
pool_tiles.normal_convention: OpenGL (+Y up, green = up), the three.js default
pool_tiles.normal_convention_verified: G channel correlates 0.967 with the source height-map gradient (positive = OpenGL)
pool_tiles.notes: Exactly 12x12 tiles per texture. Map 1 repeat to 0.6 m for 5 cm mosaic or 1.2 m for 10 cm tiles. ambientCG gives no physical size.

rubber.description: Red EPDM rubberised surface (running-track or playground rubber). Tint it for other playground colours.
rubber.author: Charlotte Baglioni
rubber.normal_convention: OpenGL (+Y up, green = up), the three.js default
rubber.normal_convention_verified: G channel correlates 0.621 with the source height-map gradient (positive = OpenGL)

wood_planks.description: Brown wooden planks for benches and pergolas.
wood_planks.author: Amal Kumar
wood_planks.normal_convention: OpenGL (+Y up, green = up), the three.js default
wood_planks.normal_convention_verified: G channel correlates 0.705 with the source height-map gradient (positive = OpenGL)
wood_planks.notes: All boards butt-join at the left/right tile edge, so a joint line appears once per repeat along the boards. Map 1 repeat per board length on bench slats and beams.

metal_painted.description: Dark powder-coated or painted steel (anthracite or black), for railings, bench frames, lamp posts and bollards.
metal_painted.author: ambientCG (Lennart Demes)
metal_painted.normal_convention: OpenGL (+Y up, green = up), the three.js default
metal_painted.normal_convention_verified: G channel correlates 0.678 with the source height-map gradient (positive = OpenGL)
metal_painted.notes: The ambientCG metalness map is a uniform 1.0 (fully metallic) and was not copied. Use metalness=1 for a coated-steel sheen or metalness=0 for a matte painted (dielectric) look. No AO in the source. No physical size given; about 1 m is suggested.

water.description: Tiling water normal map from the three.js examples, for THREE.Water (waterNormals) in pools.
water.author: three.js authors
water.normal_convention: tangent-space normal map as used by the three.js Water examples. There is no height map to verify the Y sign; use it as the examples do.
water.notes: Unmodified copy. MIT: keep the three.js copyright and permission notice (reproduced in assets/CREDITS_media.md).

files.author: ambientCG (Lennart Demes)
files.notes: Albedo/base colour. Set texture.colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace. Re-encoded from the source JPG (q85 progressive).

files.author: ambientCG (Lennart Demes)
files.notes: Tangent-space normal map, OpenGL convention (+Y), which three.js expects: use normalScale (1, 1). The source was ambientCG *_NormalGL / Poly Haven nor_gl. Re-encoded from the source JPG (q90 4:4:4 progressive).

files.author: ambientCG (Lennart Demes)
files.notes: Grayscale roughness (linear). three.js reads the G channel, and a grayscale JPEG decodes with R=G=B. Re-encoded from the source JPG (q85 progressive, converted to 1-channel grayscale).

files.notes: Grayscale ambient occlusion (linear). three.js reads the R channel; since r151 aoMap uses the primary UVs (texture.channel = 0). Re-encoded from the source JPG (q85 progressive, converted to 1-channel grayscale).
